anti_overlap: Focuses on temporal re-entry and async bridging; fd-nav-spatial-wayfinding handles structural navigation; fd-nav-annotation-flow handles review mechanics.
decision_lens: Re-entering a garden after an absence should feel like returning to a room — you should immediately see what changed while you were away.
focus: How the product handles re-entry, async gaps, and session history — what happens when you come back?
name: fd-nav-session-continuity
persona: An async collaboration product designer with experience in tools that bridge synchronous and asynchronous work (Linear, GitHub, Slack).
review_areas: When a user returns to a garden, is there a 'what changed since you left' briefing?
Are pending proposals that arrived while the user was away surfaced prominently, or buried in the list?
Is there a notification or pull model for knowing when to return to a garden?
Can users see session history — who was here, what happened, what decisions were made?
Is there a clear distinction between 'garden is actively being tended' and 'garden is idle'?
Does the product signal when async review is needed vs when real-time collaboration is happening?

severity_examples.scenario: User returns after 24 hours and sees the same view as if they never left — no 'what's new' signal
Proposals from overnight agent work are mixed into the same list as old reviewed proposals — no recency signal

severity_examples.condition: No external notification of pending review
severity_examples.scenario: User has no way to know a garden needs attention without opening it

success_hints: Returning to a garden feels like opening your email — you immediately see what's new, what needs your attention, and what happened while you were away.
task_context: Review the Garden Salon session model for continuity and async collaboration — does the product support coming back after an absence?
